column1: # The timeline divergence corpus: the series where ical-rs deliberately answers
# something recurring-ical-events 3.9.0 does not. Four tab-separated fields:
# the calendar, the UID, the occurrences ical-rs yields (as in agreement.tsv),
# and why that is the answer.
# Hand-curated, unlike agreement.tsv beside it: each line was read against the
# calendar and settled on 2026-10-29. The oracle also refuses one calendar
# no series of its own and so has no line.

column4: UNTL=, a misspelt part, is ignored as RFC 5545 3.3.10 requires of an unknown part, so the weekly rule runs unbounded; the oracle refuses the whole calendar.

The VTIMEZONE states two dated onsets, the last on 2019-03-31, and no TZUNTIL: past it ical-rs keeps the last offset (+0200) every winter, as a zone with one observance holds its offset forever; the oracle reads Europe/Berlin from the database.
One UID shared by a VEVENT and a VTODO is one series, the highest SEQUENCE (here the last listed of equals) being it; the oracle yields one occurrence per component.
DTSTART is a date and DTEND a date-time (RFC 5545 3.8.2.2 wants the same type): the same instants, the start kept a date; the oracle promotes it to a date-time.
DTSTART a date, DTEND a date-time: the same instants, the start kept a date; the oracle promotes it to a date-time.
DTSTART a date with an hours-only DURATION: the same instants, the start kept a date; the oracle promotes it to a date-time.
DTSTART a date, DTEND a UTC date-time: the same instants, the start kept a date and read floating; the oracle promotes both to UTC.
DTSTART floating, DTEND in UTC: the same instants, the start read floating as its own clock says; the oracle reads both on UTC.
DTSTART a date, DUE a date-time: the same instants, the start kept a date; the oracle promotes it to a date-time.
DTSTART a date with an hours-only DURATION: the same instants, the start kept a date; the oracle promotes it to a date-time.
DTSTART a date, DUE a UTC date-time: the same instants, the start kept a date and read floating; the oracle promotes both to UTC.
DTSTART floating, DUE in UTC: the same instants, the start read floating as its own clock says; the oracle reads both on UTC.
